status: Sample host (device c1) with records/invitation.json (camera, viewer) and records/invitation.scorer.json; join requests patch records/join-request.json; host nonces are per attempt

secrets.note: Sample secrets derived from public strings; not credentials. A real host keeps tokens in its secure store.

cases.why: Proof checks, the host challenges, the guest reveals, both screens show the same code, host approves, single use consumed
The same token presented again after use is refused and exposes nothing
A second presentation while one is pending is refused
One second after expiry on the host's own clock
Exactly at expiresAt is still valid
Approval after expiry is refused
A request for another session
A request bound to another host epoch
The guest observed a different TLS key than the QR pinned
Knowing the display code is not knowing the token
A proof made for one guest key fails for another
A proof made for one commitment fails for another
The invitation's role is the role; a guest cannot ask for more
No such invitation
The host did not confirm matching verification codes
D3: a reveal that does not open the commitment fails the attempt; nothing is pending afterwards
A reveal without a challenged join is refused
D3: the code depends on a host nonce chosen after the guest committed, so it cannot be precomputed from the QR
D11: three declined attempts by token holders revoke the invitation; no endless approval prompts
D17: a member cannot join again under a second invitation (no implicit role upgrade)
The host's own key cannot be enrolled as a guest
A new host epoch revokes every open invitation
A display code finds an invitation for host approval; it never authenticates
D11: five misses throttle that source for a 10-minute window; other sources and the code itself keep working
D18: an expired invitation is never found, even before anything else marks it

Before sending anything the guest checks roles, lifetime, endpoints and the pinned key; a QR is never a URL. The joiner never compares its own clock with the host's (D14): expiry is the host's decision
D15: every port decodes the same bytes the same way: base64url alphabet, no padding, no duplicate keys, canonical JSON only
D16: a resolved DNS-SD address passes the same LAN allow-list and port rule before connecting
